questions: If there is no path from vertex 1 to vertex N after assigning weights, what should be the output? (e.g., a sentinel like -1, or a large value, or treat as infinite distance?)
Are multiple edges between the same pair of vertices allowed? (The constraints don't forbid it, and edges are listed individually.)

Should the shortest distance be computed as the sum of weights (0 or 1) along the path, or as the number of edges? (The problem says 'weights' and 'change their weights to 1', implying sum of weights.)
Is the graph guaranteed to be simple (no self-loops) beyond u_j != v_j? (Self-loops are excluded, but parallel edges may exist.)
When choosing exactly K edges to set to 1, can we choose any K edges, or must they be distinct? (Implied distinct since edges are listed individually.)
Does the shortest distance consider only simple paths, or can paths with cycles be allowed? (Typically shortest paths in graphs with non-negative weights are simple.)
If multiple shortest paths exist, do we consider the maximum possible value over all choices of K edges? (The problem asks for maximum possible value of the shortest distance.)
Are the edges directed? (Yes, stated as directed graph.)
